basic_information.name: Cursor
basic_information.creator: Anysphere (founded 2022 by Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Arvid Lunnemark, and Aman Sanger — all MIT alumni)
basic_information.description: Cursor is an AI-native code editor built as a fork of VS Code that deeply integrates LLM-powered assistance into every stage of the development workflow. Unlike traditional coding assistants that bolt AI on top of an existing editor, Cursor was designed from the ground up with AI at its core — featuring agent mode for autonomous multi-file edits, semantic codebase indexing via RAG, intelligent tab completion, and multi-model support. For entrepreneurs, Cursor represents the developer-side of 'vibe coding': the ability to go from an idea to a working prototype dramatically faster, even with limited engineering resources. It reached $1B ARR faster than any SaaS company in history, signaling a massive shift in how software gets built.
basic_information.release_date: March 2023 (initial release); continuous updates throughout 2024-2025; Cursor 2.0 in late 2025

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-provider: OpenAI (GPT-5, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude Opus 4.1, Claude Sonnet 4), Google (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash), plus Cursor's own custom models for tab completion and embeddings. 'Auto' mode intelligently selects the best model per query based on complexity and server load.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: code-extension — Users can customize via .cursorrules files (project-level AI behavior rules), custom documentation references, MCP integrations for external tools, and VS Code extensions. Power users can configure model selection, privacy modes, and agent behavior. Not fine-tuning in the traditional sense, but deep workflow customization.
technical_capabilities.input_types: text, code files, images (for UI-to-code), documentation URLs, entire codebase context via semantic indexing, terminal output, git diffs
technical_capabilities.output_types: code (multi-file generation and editing), terminal commands (auto-executed in agent mode), code explanations, refactoring suggestions, bug fixes, architecture plans, git commits
technical_capabilities.api_access: No public API for external programmatic use. Cursor is a desktop application (Electron-based). However, it supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) for connecting to external data sources and APIs within the editor.
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Desktop application only (macOS, Windows, Linux). Cloud-only for AI inference — all LLM calls go through Cursor's servers or directly to model providers. No self-hosted AI option. Code stays local on the developer's machine (with Privacy Mode enabled).
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: multi-provider with bring-your-own-key option — Users can select from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google models. Auto mode handles model routing automatically. Users can also configure API keys for direct model provider access. No vendor lock-in on the model layer.

user_experience.target_user: developer — Primary audience is professional developers (individual and team), but increasingly adopted by technical entrepreneurs and 'vibe coders' who have basic coding literacy. Not suitable for pure non-technical users (requires understanding of code concepts).
user_experience.learning_curve: minutes (for VS Code users) to hours (for new developers) — Familiar VS Code interface means existing developers are productive immediately. The AI features (agent mode, composer, rules) take a few hours to master effectively.
user_experience.setup_time: 5-10 minutes from download to first AI-assisted code generation. Import VS Code settings and extensions in one click.
user_experience.collaboration_features: Teams plan includes shared chat threads, reusable AI rules (.cursorrules shared via git), Slack integration, shared codebase indexing (reuse teammate's index to skip indexing time on large repos), role-based access in Enterprise plan.
user_experience.template_library: Cursor Directory (cursor.directory) offers community-contributed .cursorrules templates for various frameworks and languages. Official learning hub at cursor.com/learn provides guided tutorials. No traditional project templates like no-code tools, but rules files serve a similar purpose for AI behavior.
user_experience.visual_builder_type: code-editor — AI-enhanced code editor with inline suggestions, chat panel, and agent mode. No drag-and-drop visual builder. The 'visual' element is seeing AI-generated code diffs that you accept/reject.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: Advanced built-in RAG pipeline: automatic codebase indexing using custom embedding model and AST-based semantic chunking. Files are split into meaningful units (functions, classes, ~500 token blocks), vectorized, and stored in Turbopuffer vector database. Supports @docs references to 30+ official documentation sources plus custom URLs. @codebase searches the entire project semantically. Team plan allows shared index reuse for instant onboarding on large repos.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-step autonomous — Agent mode autonomously explores the codebase, creates and edits multiple files, runs terminal commands, reads error output, and self-corrects. Subagents run in parallel for complex tasks. Composer mode handles high-level task descriptions (e.g., 'create a login page and connect it to the API') by planning architecture and generating multiple files simultaneously. Can execute shell commands, run tests, and iterate until the task passes.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor with per-query flexibility. Users can manually select models or use Auto mode. Available providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google. Model switching mid-conversation is supported. Usage-based billing means premium models cost more credits. Users can also bring their own API keys for direct provider access.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: .cursorrules files serve as persistent system prompts per project — define coding style, framework conventions, and AI behavior rules. Community-maintained rule library at cursor.directory. No built-in prompt versioning system, but rules files are version-controlled via git.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: VS Code extension ecosystem (most VS Code extensions work), MCP (Model Context Protocol) for external tool connections (Jira, Google Drive, Slack, databases via MCP servers), Git/GitHub native integration, terminal integration, Docker support via extensions, CI/CD pipeline hooks, Slack (Teams plan), custom documentation URL references
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: Inherits the full VS Code Marketplace (~40,000+ extensions), though some Microsoft-specific extensions may not activate in the fork. MCP ecosystem adds growing number of external tool connectors.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Yes — full MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for connecting AI to external data sources and APIs. Supports community MCP servers for services like Ragie (knowledge management), databases, project management tools, and cloud services. MCP enables agent interoperability and reduces vendor lock-in.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: No native webhook support as a standalone feature. However, MCP integrations and terminal access allow triggering external services. Enterprise plan may include custom integration options.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Code files (any language), git repositories, terminal output. As a code editor, the 'export' is the code itself — deployable to any platform. No proprietary format lock-in.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: freemium with usage-based premium model credits — Free Hobby tier with limited requests. Paid plans include a monthly credit pool for premium model usage (billed at API-equivalent rates). Annual billing offers 20% discount across all paid tiers.
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: Hobby (free) plan: limited number of Agent requests and Tab completions per month. Enough to evaluate the product but insufficient for daily professional use. Access to basic models only; premium models (Claude Opus, GPT-5) require paid plan.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Pro: $20/month ($16/month annual) — unlimited Tab completion, unlimited Auto mode, $20 in premium model credits. Pro+: $60/month — higher credit allocation, priority access. Ultra: $200/month — 20x more model usage, priority features. Teams: $40/user/month — shared workspaces, admin controls, shared indexing. Enterprise: custom pricing — SSO, SAML, audit logs, dedicated support, advanced security.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: No — proprietary (closed-source). Built on the open-source VS Code (MIT license) but Cursor's AI layer, custom models, and editor modifications are proprietary. The community .cursorrules ecosystem is open.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: Not available for self-hosting. Desktop app runs locally but all AI inference goes through Cursor's cloud servers (or model provider APIs). Enterprise plan may offer dedicated infrastructure but not true self-hosting.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: Primary servers in US (AWS), with latency-critical services in Europe and Singapore. Privacy Mode available: when enabled, zero data retention by model providers, no code used for training. SOC 2 certified, GDPR compliant. Without Privacy Mode (accounts after Oct 15, 2025): prompts may be shared with model providers. Enterprise plan offers additional security controls. No explicit EU-only hosting option documented.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Undisputed leader in AI-native code editors. Reached $1B ARR faster than any SaaS company in history. Valued at $29.3B (Nov 2025), making it one of the most valuable AI startups globally alongside OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI. Dominates the individual developer and small team segment; rapidly expanding into enterprise.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Salesforce (20,000 developers, 90%+ adoption, double-digit improvements in cycle time), Coinbase (100% engineer adoption, single engineers doing in days what took months), Stripe (thousands of employees), OpenAI, Midjourney, Perplexity, Shopify. Over 40,000 paying enterprise customers. Fortune 500 companies actively using Cursor for production development.
adoption_and_market.community_size: 1 million+ daily active users (Dec 2025), 360,000+ paying customers, 40,000+ enterprise customers. Active community forum at forum.cursor.com. Cursor Directory (cursor.directory) for community rules and learning resources. Not open-source, so no GitHub stars for the main product. 9,900% year-over-year ARR growth.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: ~$3.4B across 4 rounds. Seed (Oct 2023): $8M led by OpenAI Startup Fund. Series A (Aug 2024): $60M led by a16z at $400M valuation. Series B (Jan 2025): $105M at $2.5B valuation. Series C (Jun 2025): $900M led by Thrive Capital at $9.9B valuation. Series D (Nov 2025): $2.3B led by Accel and Coatue at $29.3B valuation. Strategic investors include Google and Nvidia. ARR surpassed $1B by late 2025.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: GitHub Copilot (Microsoft/GitHub — largest installed base, deep GitHub integration, $19-39/mo), Windsurf (Codeium — lower price at $10-15/mo, Supercomplete feature), Claude Code (Anthropic — terminal-based, strong for autonomous coding), Replit Agent (browser-based, targets non-developers), Cline/Roo Code (open-source VS Code extensions). Key differentiators: AI-native architecture (not a plugin), multi-model flexibility, agent mode autonomy, codebase-wide RAG, and fastest innovation velocity.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: low to medium — Code is standard, exportable, and not in a proprietary format. VS Code settings/extensions mostly transfer. However, .cursorrules files are Cursor-specific, team workflows built around Cursor's agent mode don't transfer, and the AI-assisted development experience creates soft lock-in (developers become dependent on the AI assistance). Switching to another editor means losing the AI workflow, not the code.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea: Project 1 (45 min): 'Build a Landing Page from a Napkin Sketch' — Students sketch a startup landing page on paper, take a photo, and use Cursor's agent mode to generate a complete HTML/CSS/JS landing page from the image. They then iterate with natural language ('add a pricing section', 'make the CTA button more prominent', 'add a contact form that saves to localStorage'). Demonstrates vibe coding and the speed of AI-assisted prototyping. Project 2 (90 min): 'From Idea to API in 90 Minutes' — Students define a simple business API (e.g., a product catalog or booking system) using natural language descriptions in Cursor's composer mode. The agent generates a complete Flask/FastAPI backend with endpoints, data models, and basic tests. Students then deploy to a free service (Render, Railway). Teaches the full cycle from idea to deployed MVP, showcasing how a non-CTO founder could validate a technical concept.
teaching_and_classroom.tutorial_resources: Official: https://cursor.com/docs/get-started/quickstart (quickstart guide), https://cursor.com/learn (interactive learning hub). Community: https://cursor.directory/learn (curated tutorials and rules). Courses: Codecademy 'Intro to AI Coding with Cursor' (free, <1 hour, absolute beginners), Udemy 'Cursor AI for Beginners: AI Coding Crash Course'. Articles: TechTarget step-by-step tutorial (https://www.techtarget.com/searchenterpriseai/tutorial/Get-started-with-Cursor-AI-A-step-by-step-tutorial), Geeky Gadgets beginner guide (https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/cursor-ai-coding-guide/). Forum: https://forum.cursor.com (active community forum with guides section).
teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: basic prompting + minimal coding concepts — Students need to understand what code is and basic file/folder concepts. No Python or JavaScript required for vibe coding projects (the AI writes the code). Basic prompting skills help get better results from the agent. Familiarity with VS Code is helpful but not required.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools): demonstrate vibe coding as the developer-side complement to no-code tools; show how prompt engineering applies to code generation. Session 3 (AI Project Frameworks): use Cursor to prototype an MVP as part of Build vs Buy discussion; demonstrate how AI tools change the economics of building custom solutions. Session 4 (AI Business Models): discuss Cursor's business model as a case study ($0 to $1B ARR in 2 years, usage-based pricing evolution, multi-model strategy).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Cursor is relevant from day zero of a technical startup. Pre-seed/Seed stage: solo founders or small teams (1-3 people) can use Cursor to build MVPs at 3-10x the speed of traditional development. A non-CTO founder with basic coding literacy can prototype features and validate ideas before hiring engineers. Series A+: engineering teams adopt Cursor to increase developer velocity — Coinbase reported single engineers doing in days what previously took months. The $20/mo Pro plan is trivially affordable for any startup. Best fit: startups where speed-to-market matters more than architectural perfection, and where the founding team has at least one person comfortable with code concepts.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Hours to days for simple web apps (landing pages, CRUD APIs, chatbots). 1-2 weeks for more complex MVPs (multi-page apps with authentication, databases, third-party integrations). Cursor's agent mode can generate entire features from natural language descriptions, dramatically compressing the idea-to-prototype cycle. The key bottleneck shifts from writing code to clearly specifying what you want.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Cursor when: you need custom functionality that no-code tools can't provide, you want full control over your codebase, you plan to scale the engineering team later, or your product IS software. Use no-code tools instead when: you need a standard workflow (chatbot, form, automation) that tools like Voiceflow or Make handle out-of-the-box, you have zero coding experience and no desire to learn, or you need to ship in hours not days. Key insight: Cursor occupies a middle ground — it's not no-code (you still work with code), but it dramatically lowers the bar for who can write production-quality software. Cost comparison: $20/mo for Cursor vs. $50-500/mo for enterprise no-code tools, but Cursor requires more technical skill.
key_lessons: 1. Vibe coding is real but requires skill: Cursor makes coding 3-10x faster, but the quality of output depends heavily on how well you describe what you want. Prompt engineering for code is a distinct skill — learning to write good .cursorrules and clear task descriptions is the new competitive advantage.

2. The $0-to-$1B ARR playbook: Cursor grew entirely through product-led growth and word-of-mouth. No enterprise sales team was needed initially. Lesson for entrepreneurs: if your product genuinely makes people more productive, growth can be explosive without traditional marketing.

3. Multi-model strategy reduces risk: Cursor's support for multiple AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) means it isn't dependent on any single model. Entrepreneurs building AI products should consider similar multi-provider architectures to avoid vendor lock-in and always access the best available model.

4. AI changes Build vs Buy economics: With Cursor, 'building' custom software becomes dramatically cheaper and faster, which shifts the break-even point of build-vs-buy analysis. Startups should reassess whether off-the-shelf solutions are still worth their premium when custom development is 5-10x cheaper than before.

5. Usage-based pricing is the future of AI tools: Cursor's June 2025 shift from flat-rate to credit-based pricing (aligned with actual AI compute costs) is a pattern every AI startup should study. It aligns revenue with value delivered and scales naturally with user engagement.

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from CNBC, TechCrunch, Crunchbase, official Cursor documentation, and multiple independent reviews from 2025-2026. Funding and valuation data confirmed across multiple financial news sources.
confidence.cross_reference: Funding data confirmed by CNBC, TechCrunch, Crunchbase, TechFundingNews, and SiliconANGLE. Feature information verified across official docs, DigitalOcean comparison, Builder.io review, and NxCode 6-month review. Pricing confirmed via official cursor.com/pricing and multiple third-party pricing analyses. Customer data from Contrary Research, Opsera adoption analysis, and company announcements.
confidence.caveats: Cursor's pricing and feature set evolve rapidly (near-weekly updates in 2025). The June 2025 pricing shift from flat-rate to usage-based was controversial and may continue evolving. Some VS Code extensions may not work due to Microsoft's fork-detection code. Privacy Mode is opt-in, and default behavior for post-Oct 2025 accounts shares data with model providers. The $29.3B valuation reflects private market dynamics and may not reflect sustainable value. Enterprise features and exact model availability change frequently.
